verdict.line: You lose if Jayce free-hits you with Hammer-stance leaps and Cannon Shock Blast before level 6; you win if you survive to six and land R on him while he's stuck in Cannon stance.

brief.thesis: Jayce's whole advantage lives in the gap his Hammer Q leap, E knockback, and Cannon Shock Blast create before you have a reliable way to close it. R (All Out) is the one tool that erases that gap outright, but it isn't live until level 6 and sits on a long 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown. Lane around surviving that poke window with your shields and sustain, and the matchup flips hard the moment he's forced to stand still near you.

theirWindow.when: Jayce in Cannon stance with Q up
theirWindow.what: In Cannon stance with Shock Blast (Q) available, Jayce can detonate the orb on you for free poke damage; hold behind minions and don't commit forward until it's on cooldown.

yourWindow.when: Your R is up and he's exposed
yourWindow.what: The instant R (All Out) comes off cooldown, look for Jayce in Cannon stance or just after he's fired Shock Blast — knock him through terrain and dash in before his range advantage resets.

powerCurve.note: Jayce's leap-knockback poke outranges your tools

All Out closes gap, catches Cannon form
Tank core and sustain overwhelm his poke

start.why: Highest measured start at 49.8% over 2,546 games and the most picked option (72%); the extra magic resist and sustain soak the chip from his E (Thundering Blow) and Hammer Q leap while you farm Q stacks.

boots.why: 48.2% win rate over 2,945 games at an 86% pick rate; cuts down the auto-attack and on-hit chip Jayce stacks in both stances.

core.why: Anchors the highest-win-rate core path (52.3% over 237 games); the on-hit slow is what lets you actually stick to Jayce once R closes the gap, and the mana fixes K'Sante's early resource problems.
Omnivamp and flat armor keep you topped up through his poke phase instead of just surviving it.
Stacking resistances scale into the extended fights K'Sante wants, and the ability haste shortens your R and E cooldowns.

situational.when: the enemy team has a crit-heavy or attack-speed carry stacking with Jayce
Jayce or an ally is building heavy on-hit or lifesteal sustain
his E (Thundering Blow) and R procs' magic damage start adding up alongside another magic source

runes.keystoneWhy: Triggers the instant you immobilize Jayce with W's stun or R's knockback, handing you bonus resistances right as you all-in — useful since his burst only has short windows to land.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 84.4% of games at 47.5% win rate and lets you reset after losing the early poke war; Flash+Ignite is the higher-win-rate alternative (52.3% over a smaller sample) if you want to press the lane's solo-kill advantage once R is up.

playing.title: Respect Cannon-stance poke
playing.detail: Before level 6, don't walk up while Jayce is in Cannon stance holding Q — Shock Blast detonates on hit for physical damage, and you have no reliable way to close that distance yet.

playing.title: Farm Q stacks on wave
playing.detail: Hit minions with Q (Ntofo Strikes) whenever it's safe; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls Jayce in, giving you a free engage even without R up.

playing.title: All-in the second R is up
playing.detail: At level 6, use R (All Out) the moment Jayce is in Cannon stance or has just fired Shock Blast — the knockback sends him through terrain and your dash finally closes the range he's been denying you.

playing.title: Charge W into his pokes
playing.detail: W (Path Maker)'s channel takes reduced damage, so start charging it into his Hammer Q leap or E knockback to blunt the trade before you dash.

playing.title: Punish Hammer-stance melee windows
playing.detail: When Jayce swaps to Hammer stance to farm or trade in melee, his range advantage disappears — step in with Q and autos immediately.

playing.title: Build through the poke, not around it
playing.detail: Rush Iceborn Gauntlet into Unending Despair; the slow and omnivamp let you stay attached and sustain through Shock Blast chip once you're in his face.

playing.title: Track his R's 6s cooldown
playing.detail: Jayce's R only costs 6 seconds and swaps stances freely — don't assume he's locked out of Cannon range just because he's in Hammer stance; he can flip back before your next engage.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the power-curve timing and trade reasoning are my own read on the mechanics, not measured data.
